{"content":"Investigated the regression in `Statement.get_type()` in sqlparse/sql.py. The bug was an inverted condition: `elif token.ttype != T.Keyword.CTE:` caused the WITH-clause-scanning logic (which looks past the CTE definitions for the actual DML keyword) to be skipped precisely when the first token *is* the CTE keyword (i.e., for `WITH ... SELECT ...` statements) — the exact opposite of the intended behavior. This made `get_type()` return `'UNKNOWN'` instead of `'SELECT'` for any statement starting with `WITH`, including cases with comments between CTE clauses.

Fixed by changing the condition to `elif token.ttype == T.Keyword.CTE:`, which is correct: when the first token is the CTE keyword, scan forward past the Identifier/IdentifierList of CTE definitions to find the following DML keyword and return it.

Verified manually:

Investigated the regression in `Statement.get_type()` in sqlparse/sql.py. The bug was an inverted condition: `elif token.ttype != T.Keyword.CTE:` caused the WITH-clause-scanning logic (which looks past the CTE definitions for the actual DML keyword) to be skipped precisely when the first token *is* the CTE keyword (i.e., for `WITH ... SELECT ...` statements) — the exact opposite of the intended behavior. This made `get_type()` return `'UNKNOWN'` instead of `'SELECT'` for any statement starting with `WITH`, including cases with comments between CTE clauses.

Fixed by changing the condition to `elif token.ttype == T.Keyword.CTE:`, which is correct: when the first token is the CTE keyword, scan forward past the Identifier/IdentifierList of CTE definitions to find the following DML keyword and return it.

Verified manually:
- `WITH x AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM x` → `get_type()` now returns `'SELECT'` (fixes 'issue227 gettype cte').
- `WITH a AS (SELECT 1), -- comment\nb AS (SELECT 2) SELECT * FROM a,b` → `get_type()` now returns `'SELECT'` (fixes 'comment between cte clauses issue632'), since the inner loop already tolerates comment tokens by continuing to advance until it finds the Identifier/IdentifierList and subsequent DML keyword.

No local test suite exists in this checkout (only sqlparse source and docs are present; the `tests/` directory has been stripped out), so I verified behavior via direct Python invocation of `sqlparse.parse(...)[0].get_type()` for both scenarios described in the bug report, plus confirmed non-CTE statements are unaffected (DML/DDL-first tokens still short-circuit before reaching this branch, and empty statements still return `'UNKNOWN'`).
